determinism.description: Each gating value read from the plane that owns it; the no-pair exemption verified at its source rather than inherited from the order; both plans graded at the resource-block grain with a positive control; and the failing tier kept as evidence rather than discarded.
determinism.method: (i) the live base read before the edit (MemorySize, Timeout, CodeSha256) and the terraform value read beside it, so file and world were compared before touching either; (ii) CTO round-61 addendum ruling 5 read at f1d5dac151 to confirm the track-A no-pair classification in the CTO's own words; (iii) each plan saved and the SAVED plan applied, with the changed-attribute lines counted rather than eyeballed; (iv) live MemorySize and CodeSha256 read back after each apply, not taken from the apply rc; (v) AC1 run at BOTH tiers, the failing one committed alongside the passing one; (vi) max memory used and Init Duration read out of the same REPORT lines the durations come from.
determinism.expected: (i) 1769 in both file and world; (ii) the ruling classes track A config-only with no pair; (iii) one resource, memory_size only, at each step; (iv) MemorySize moves and CodeSha256 does not; (v) a verdict at each tier; (vi) figures that explain the result rather than only report it.
determinism.observed: All hold. (i) live MemorySize 1769 / Timeout 29 / CodeSha256 E+FAZF0f... and scoped-amgt-api.tf:326 memory_size = 1769 -- file and world agreed, and the hash being ak-2's confirms nothing had redeployed this function since 07:45Z. (ii) ruling 5 reads 'config only; no served value moves, so no never-widen pair. Rollback: the memory back to 1769' -- the CTO's words, so the exemption is the ruling's and not an issuer inference. (iii) each plan: 'Plan: 0 to add, 1 to change, 0 to destroy', 1 planned resource block, exactly 1 changed attribute line (1769 -> 3538, then 3538 -> 10240); source_code_hash 0, s3_object_version 0, must-be-replaced 0, will-be-destroyed 0, forces-replacement 0, aws_lambda_alias 0, positive control memory_size non-zero. (iv) MemorySize 3538 then 10240; CodeSha256 identical throughout. (v) C1 FAIL at 3538 (21726.76 / 20439.58 / 22913.08 ms), C1 PASS at 10240 (16885.18 / 16551.67 / 19105.13 ms). (vi) max memory USED 455-463 MB at every tier, moving 8 MB across a 5.8x raise, and Init Duration 157-204 ms, about 0.9 percent of elapsed. ACT (B) ADDS ITS OWN READS. (vii) The pre-build and pre-upload guards checked THREE live values as one mechanical abort -- CodeSha256, MemorySize AND the artifact VersionId -- because act (A) had set MemorySize 10240 forty minutes earlier under a DIFFERENT entry, so act (B) had to prove it was building on that state rather than assume it; all three matched. (viii) CONTENT-DIFF recomputed from both artifacts by member sha256: 350/350 members, IDENTICAL 349, CHANGED 1, set equal to [lib/research/api/scoped_amgt.py] both ways, fabricated-path control discriminating; the graded zip's sha256 equals the uploaded content-sha256, so the grade covers the bytes that landed. (ix) The plan's decisive feature was an ABSENCE: memory_size did not appear as a changed attribute, which is what proves act (B) did not silently revert act (A)'s signed value -- and the post-apply live read confirms MemorySize 10240. (x) The pre file was NOT re-run, on the order's own test: AL2_CONTROLS_PRE.json carries CodeSha256 E+FAZF0f... and MemorySize 10240, so it postdates act (A) and is current.

mutant.description: The base arm is the incident itself, and this act carries a REAL failing arm rather than a hypothetical one.
mutant.expected: Per the order's preflight, AC1's C0 FAILS at the base (MemorySize unmoved) and the route times out cold at 1769 against the 29 s ceiling; CVO~Z measured 5 cold timeouts at 10Z (row Z-C-S29).
mutant.observed: The discriminator is not a planted mutant here, it is the 3538 tier: the SAME criterion, the SAME invocation, read C1 FAIL 0 of 3 at 3538 and C1 PASS 3 of 3 at 10240, about three minutes apart, with C0 and C2 passing in both. That is a measured negative arm on the live system, which is stronger than a simulated one, and it is why the 10240 landing is an escalation rather than a guess that happened to work. Both outputs are committed. A SECOND, UNASKED-FOR READ sharpens it: memory USED never exceeded 463 MB at any tier, so the knob was never relieving memory pressure -- it buys vCPU, and the improvement from 27 s at 1769 to 21 s at 3538 to 17 s at 10240 tracks vCPU, not headroom. ACT (B) CARRIES THE STRONGEST ARM OF THE SESSION, and it was not planted: the new deadline branch FIRED IN PRODUCTION during its own acceptance run. Run 3 returned 200 at 18006.03 ms carrying headline_reason True -- 6 ms past TIMELINE_SILVER_DEADLINE_S = 18.0 -- while runs 1 and 2 at 16532.87 and 15135.96 ms took the normal path. So the live grade exercised BOTH branches of the change in one run, and the planted-slow pytest (3 passed) independently proves the branch behaves correctly when forced. L4 says the branch behaves; L3 says it fires; neither alone would establish the other, which is why the CTO condition names both.

declared_exclusions.item: There is no never-widen pair for this act, and that is the ruling's decision rather than this seat's.
declared_exclusions.reason: CTO round-61 addendum ruling 5 @f1d5dac151 classes track A 'config only; no served value moves, so no never-widen pair'. This seat read the ruling rather than relying on the order's restatement of it, because CLAUDE.md's first NEVER forbids moving served output without the pair and 'no pair needed' is exactly the claim to confirm upstream. AC1's C2 is the standing evidence that nothing served moved: the AMD control day's body sha256 is byte-identical to its pre value at both tiers.

declared_exclusions.item: AC1's C1 is measured on ONE route, ONE day and ONE name (BA /timeline/day/2026-09-08), with 3 invokes.
declared_exclusions.reason: That is the criterion as written and it is the demo-risk path the incident was reported on. It is not a statement about the route's behaviour on other names or heavier days, and the margin recorded in row AMGT_RESAPP-Z-S336 is why that distinction matters: the slowest passing run clears the 20 s target by 895 ms.

declared_exclusions.item: The pre probe in this seat's own run read BA WARM at 528.41 ms, while the order's preflight records 27,194 ms WARM at the same memory.
declared_exclusions.reason: Both are warm reads at 1769 MB and they differ by roughly 50x, so 'warm' is plainly not one state for this route -- a repeatedly-warm sandbox with the day's data already in process is not the same as the first warm call after a deploy. It did not change the act, because AC1 grades COLD invokes and the incident is a cold-path timeout, and this seat had no license to profile the route. Recorded rather than smoothed over, because anyone comparing the two pre numbers will otherwise think one of them is wrong.

declared_exclusions.item: Why the remaining 16-19 s is spent was not measured.
declared_exclusions.reason: Out of scope: BOUNDS 1 is the one property and nothing else, and profiling the handler is ruling 5's track C (stop reading whole-publisher silver), which is scheduled after the demo. Row AMGT_RESAPP-Z-S336 states this as unmeasured rather than implying the cause is known.

declared_exclusions.item: comp-iam and comp-schedule were not run.
declared_exclusions.reason: Both are DECLARED-NOT-APPLICABLE in the order's preflight: a memory_size change grants nothing and arms no cadence. The gating clause is the plan carrying no IAM change, and both plans carried exactly one changed attribute.

declared_exclusions.item: A HALTGT checkpoint pass is cited nowhere.
declared_exclusions.reason: Per /cloud-ops and LD-0267 the checkpoint sees only unread files directly under inbox/<serial>/, and a ~lane seat is unhaltable regardless. Two safe-apply invocations ran; neither pass is evidence of anything.
C2 passed at both tiers, so the rollback trigger never fired. The rollback stayed available throughout and is named by ruling 5 itself: memory_size back to 1769 through one safe-apply.

declared_exclusions.item: Act (B) carries the never-widen pair and act (A) did not, and that difference is the ruling's.
declared_exclusions.reason: Ruling 5 classes track A config-only ('no served value moves, so no never-widen pair') and track B as moving served output on the timeout path, 'so it carries the never-widen pair'. Both classifications were read at the ruling rather than inherited. Act (B)'s pair evidence is timeline_b's C2: two control days that do NOT hit the deadline came back byte-identical to their pre values, which is exactly the scope the halves signed.

declared_exclusions.item: The rate at which the deadline branch fires is measured on 3 concurrent runs and nothing larger.
declared_exclusions.reason: 1 of 3 crossed 18 s during the acceptance run, and act (A)'s AC1 an hour earlier read 16.6 / 16.9 / 19.1 s at the same memory -- so two independent runs put the cold distribution across the line. That is enough to report the branch as routinely reached and not enough to state a rate: the three runs are concurrent and share one post-deploy moment, and nothing here varies the name or the day's article count. Row AMGT_RESAPP-Z-S337 states it that way rather than quoting 33 percent as if measured.

declared_exclusions.item: The 18.0 s constant was not tuned and no rollback was taken.
declared_exclusions.reason: BOUNDS and the pair authorise one upload and one code-only apply at the signed commit; changing TIMELINE_SILVER_DEADLINE_S would be a different code change under a new pair. C1 and C2 both passed, so the rollback trigger never fired; the rollback stayed available throughout as artifact VersionId YSqlUTOWHwV6H7LePjd1pr9DKomiDo5U through one code-only safe-apply.
